sites.name: Mount Merapi and the Opak River, Central Java, Indonesia
sites.footprintNote: Summit cone and upper flanks of Merapi. The Opak River deposits downstream are not inside it.

sites.name: Gua Lawa lava tube, Purbalingga, Central Java, Indonesia

sites.footprintNote: Centred on Giri Mulyo village, because the cave's own position is not published. The cave interior is not measured.

sites.footprintNote: Centred on Batur volcano, because the tube's position inside the caldera is not published.

sites.name: Maros-Pangkep karst caves, South Sulawesi, Indonesia
sites.footprintNote: One 5 km sample of the karst at the listed coordinates, not the whole cave district.

sites.name: Mount Tambora caldera, Sumbawa, Indonesia
sites.footprintNote: The whole summit caldera of Tambora, rim to rim, with a little of the outer slope in the corners of the square.

sites.name: Mount Batur black lava fields, Bali, Indonesia
sites.footprintNote: Young bare lava flows on the caldera floor south-west of the Batur cone.
sites.caveat: The square is 16 km2 and the mapped bare-rock polygon inside it is 7.5 km2, so about half of the footprint is ground outside the lava field.

sites.name: Mauna Kea, Hawaii, USA
sites.footprintNote: Summit area of Mauna Kea. The field-test sites on the flank are outside it.

sites.name: Atacama Desert hyperarid core (Yungay), Chile
sites.footprintNote: Centred on the published approximate position (24 S, 70 W), not a surveyed station.

sites.name: Haughton impact structure, Devon Island, Canada
sites.footprintNote: Central part of the 23 km impact structure only.

sites.name: Timanfaya, Lanzarote, Spain
sites.footprintNote: Timanfaya lava field at the listed coordinates.

sites.name: Dallol, Danakil Depression, Ethiopia
sites.footprintNote: Dallol crater and hydrothermal field on the Danakil salt plain.

sites.name: Dasht-e Lut (Lut Desert), Iran
sites.footprintNote: One 5 km sample of the Lut Desert, not the whole desert.

sites.name: Salar de Uyuni salt flat, Bolivia
sites.footprintNote: One 5 km sample of the salt flat.
sites.caveat: The Copernicus DEM water body mask classes 96% of this footprint as water (the salt flat floods in the wet season) and Sentinel-2 classes most clear views of the salt as snow. Terrain on 463 m posts is therefore null, and slopeFine, roughnessFine, ndvi and bareFrac rest on the 4% of the footprint outside the mask. waterFrac here is not a measurement of open water.

sites.name: Tunupa volcano, north shore of Salar de Uyuni, Bolivia
sites.footprintNote: Summit area of Tunupa volcano. The salt flat is outside it.
